subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers repair or adopt the open linked PR as the SSRF socket-error fix, or request a fresh narrow replacement with live IPv6-unreachable proof?
rationale: The remaining work touches the SSRF security boundary and the current linked PR review identifies pinning/proxy contract blockers, so this should not be converted into a new issue-level automated fix job without maintainer direction.

options.title: Repair or replace with proof
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, require the linked PR or a replacement to preserve all pinned dispatcher modes, and ask for redacted Linux/Docker proof that the IPv6-only failure rejects without process exit.

options.title: Land after maintainer risk acceptance
options.body: A maintainer could accept a narrower source-level fix without live proof, but should explicitly own the SSRF and availability risk in the PR review.

options.title: Pause for reporter logs first
options.body: Maintainers can request the retained stack traces before reviewing implementation details if they want stronger failure-mode confirmation.

recommendation.title: Repair or replace with proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, require the linked PR or a replacement to preserve all pinned dispatcher modes, and ask for redacted Linux/Docker proof that the IPv6-only failure rejects without process exit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent SSRF/Undici dispatcher history in the files implicated by this issue.
